title: Choosing a quiet room
bodyMd:
A fictional college converted a seldom-used lounge into a silent study room. Usage rose during examinations but remained low at other times. An administrator called it inefficient because it was empty on many afternoons. Students replied that knowing a quiet place would be available when needed had value even when they did not occupy it daily.

The college considered opening the room for meetings outside examination periods. It discovered that bookings would need to be predictable: a room advertised as a dependable refuge would lose that function if students repeatedly arrived to find it unavailable. The final proposal reserved some hours for silent study year-round and allowed meetings during clearly published periods. The discussion shifted from maximizing occupancy to balancing different uses without making any promise unreliable.
